key_insight: There is no single best model for producing diverse valid answers; training a lightweight router to pick models or decoding strategies per prompt yields broader, higher-quality coverage of unique answers.
problem_solved: How to reliably generate a comprehensive set of valid responses for prompts that admit many correct answers, rather than relying on one model or one decoding run that misses important modes of the answer space.
method: Introduce a diversity-aware evaluation metric, "diversity coverage", that scores the total quality of unique answers relative to an optimal set of the same size.
Train a router that selects which model(s) or decoding strategy to use for each input, aiming to maximize diversity coverage across the collected outputs.
Aggregate outputs from the routed models to produce a final answer set with improved uniqueness and overall quality.
impact: Provides a practical way to improve coverage of valid responses in conditional generation tasks—useful for dialog, creative writing, and retrieval—by combining multiple models intelligently rather than searching for one universally best model.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing an input prompt → router → multiple models → deduplicated diverse answer set
Illustration of the "diversity coverage" concept: unique-answer quality stacked bar compared to an optimal oracle set
Bar/chart comparison: single-model vs. routed-ensemble diversity coverage across tasks
Example answer set visualization (e.g., clustered bubbles) highlighting increased unique modes after routing
paper_title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
